_comment: THE WASM TIER'S DEPLOYED TOPOLOGY -- one committed definition, read by everything.
Before this file the same list of Workers was written out by hand in four places:
scripts/stage_wasm_families.sh's build loop, .github/workflows/wasm-tier-deploy.yml's
deploy loop, tools/wasm/sweep_multi_worker.mjs's FAMILIES, and
tools/wasm/check_deployed_freshness.mjs's FAMILIES. Adding a Worker meant editing four
lists, and FORGETTING THE FOURTH IS SILENT: a Worker that is built, deployed and swept
but absent from the freshness checker is a Worker nothing ever proves is current -- the
exact shape of the 2026-08-07..2026-08-10 staleness window, reintroduced one Worker at a
time. Every one of those four consumers now reads this file, so a Worker cannot be
deployed without also being checked.
Ten Workers today: temper-drc-rs's full corpus + its 7 family shards (1719), and one
single-family Worker each for temper-geometry (722) and temper-thermal (143).
## Structure: tiers, not families
A `tier` is ONE CRATE's wasm32 corpus. It has a full-corpus Worker (every test the crate
registers) and a set of shard Workers that must partition that corpus exactly. The
freshness invariant is stated PER TIER, because the three crates are three separate
`cargo build` invocations producing three separate .wasm files with three independent
counts.
Stating it per tier rather than over the union is the point, and is strictly stronger. If
the checker only compared 1719+722+143 against a single deployed total, a +11 drift in
temper-drc-rs cancelling a -11 drift in temper-geometry would pass -- two stale modules
reported green by arithmetic. Per tier, each crate's deployed count must equal its own
built count, so nothing cancels.
## Why temper-geometry and temper-thermal are their own Workers rather than more tests
## in temper-wasm-tier
1. Each declares exactly one family (`wasm-registry-geometry`, `wasm-registry-thermal`;
see those crates' Cargo.toml): each is a flat set of independent kernels with no
rule-family taxonomy, so a per-family split has nothing to split on.
2. It leaves the existing Workers' bytes, counts, and dependency graphs untouched --
both crates are OPTIONAL dependencies of temper-wasm-test-runner precisely so a
drc-only build is unchanged. The drc invariant (temper-wasm-tier == 1719 == the sum of
its 7 shards) therefore keeps its exact prior meaning, and the control that caught the
11-test gap on 2026-08-10 keeps its exact prior bite.
3. One Worker serves both of each crate's roles: it is the tier's full-corpus Worker AND
the single shard sweep_multi_worker.mjs dispatches. So each is +1 Cloudflare script,
not +2.
Note honestly what that costs: each of those tiers' shard set is the singleton {itself},
so its partition check (`shards sum == built`) is the SAME equation as its full-corpus
check and adds nothing. The count check is the whole bite for those tiers, and it is not
degenerate. The partition check regains its independent force the day either crate is
sharded by size.
## Fields
crate              Cargo package whose registry this tier carries. Informational, and
the key callers use to name a tier on the command line.
cargo_features     --features passed to temper-wasm-test-runner to build the full
corpus for this tier. --no-default-features is always also passed.
staged_module      Filename under packages/temper-worker/src/ that
scripts/stage_wasm_families.sh copies the built .wasm to, and that
the Worker entry point imports. Gitignored (.gitignore:141).
full_corpus_worker Cloudflare script name carrying every test in the tier.
wrangler_dir       Directory containing the wrangler.toml for full_corpus_worker.
expected_failures  Manifest of native-vs-wasm32 divergences for this crate. Bundled
into the Worker and passed to run_wasm_tests.mjs / r19_compare.py.
native_test_args   The `cargo test` invocation whose verdicts this tier's wasm32
verdicts are compared against (R19). Debug, not release, for every
tier -- see "Why every native arm is debug" below.
shards             The per-family Workers. sweep_multi_worker.mjs dispatches THESE;
the full-corpus Worker is not in that fan-out at all, which is why
their counts must sum to the built count independently.
## Why every native arm is debug
temper-geometry FORCED the choice. Measured 2026-08-10 on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu:
`cargo test --release --no-default-features` fails 1 (778/1) where debug passes 779/0.
The failure is pad_geometry::tests::pow2_is_exact_where_powi_is_not, a staleness guard
asserting that LLVM does NOT fold powi(2, -1024) natively the way it does on wasm32. At
opt-level 3 it does fold, the guard fails on BOTH sides, r19_compare.py scores agree_fail,
and a real divergence stops being reported as one.
temper-thermal PERMITS release and is pinned to debug anyway. Measured 2026-08-10, same
host: `--no-default-features` passes 191/0 in BOTH profiles, and all four of its
b7-pow-divergence-absent guards pass in both. They survive -O3 because
hostmath::pow is a `dlsym`-resolved function pointer -- opaque to LLVM, so there is
nothing to constant-fold, unlike geometry's `powi` intrinsic. That immunity is a property
of hostmath.rs's current implementation, not a guarantee: the day hostmath falls back to
`f64::powf` natively (which is exactly what it already does on wasm32, and the reason
those four tests are in the manifest), release would fold and the guards would fail
natively too -- geometry's failure mode, one crate later. Debug is where the guard has
headroom, it is what the other two tiers already run, and it saves the nightly a second
full x86_64 optimised compile of the dependency graph. There is no offsetting benefit to
release here: no wasm32 verdict depends on the native profile, only the join does.
## Why every native arm is --no-default-features
For temper-thermal this is load-bearing in a way it is not for the other two: that
crate's DEFAULT feature is `python`, which pulls pyo3 (with `extension-module`) and faer
into a plain `cargo test`. Measured 2026-08-10: the default build passes 198/0 and
`--no-default-features` passes 191/0. The 7-test difference is EXACTLY
`solve::tests::*` (7 tests; the module is `#[cfg(feature = "python")]` at the crate
root, and it is the faer sparse-LU call plus its pyo3 bridge) -- nothing else differs in
either direction. The wasm32 registry cannot contain them, so those 7 are `native_only`
under EITHER invocation and comparing them is not on offer. Paying a pyo3 + faer build
every night to move 7 tests from one native_only bucket to another buys nothing; all 143
wasm32 names are present natively either way (verified: 0 wasm32_only).
